ads1 个函数
Tool namespace `ads`.
ads.resolve_entities
Required finalization tool for Ads responses that name an ad account, campaign, ad set, or ad from Ads tool results. After selecting every entity the response will name, call this tool once before composing the final response. Include every resolvable named entity, passing its name and ID exactly as returned; campaigns, ad sets, and ads also require their owning ad account ID. Copy every returned marker exactly where that entity name belongs. Do not leave one resolvable entity as plain text while citing another. If a named entity genuinely lacks a required ID, it may remain plain text; never invent names or IDs. Use numeric IDs with at most one act_ prefix. The runtime creates fallback links, so do not supply links.
出参 → 返回解析后的广告实体标记（chips），用于在回复中正确引用广告账户/系列/组/广告。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "entities": {
      "items": {
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "account_id": {
            "description": "Owning L4 ad account id, bare numerics (a single act_ prefix is accepted and stripped). Required for campaign, ad_set, and ad; omit for ad_account.",
            "minLength": 1,
            "type": "string"
          },
          "display_name": {
            "description": "Entity name exactly as returned by the Ads data source, shown on the chip.",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "entity_id": {
            "description": "Raw stable L4-L1 id of the entity, bare numerics exactly as returned by the Ads data source (a single act_ prefix is accepted and stripped).",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": {
            "description": "Ads object level. Must match the level of entity_id.",
            "enum": [
              "ad_account",
              "campaign",
              "ad_set",
              "ad"
            ],
            "type": "string"
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "type",
          "entity_id",
          "display_name"
        ],
        "type": "object"
      },
      "maxItems": 50,
      "minItems": 1,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "entities"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
artifact15 个函数
Durable artifacts: web pages and apps, editable documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets / CSV data exports, markdown files, and any other plain file type (kind `other`). Web artifacts (`web_static` and `web_fullstack`) live on the hosted web runtime; file artifacts land under `workspace/your_files/<slug>/` by default. A document for a goal takes that goal's id as `goal_id` on the create call. The tool then builds it under the goal, so it is one of that goal's documents at once. Choose the destination on the create call. Do not build elsewhere and move or copy it after. A create call picks its function by kind: a hosted web page or app is artifact.create_web_static or artifact.create_web_fullstack, and a new file deliverable is artifact.create_file. Each create function's own description carries the choice. Artifacts change only through this namespace: every feature, content, styling, fix, or debugging change to an existing artifact goes through artifact.edit (never read or edit an artifact's files directly, and never rebuild over an existing artifact with a second create), artifact.delete permanently removes an artifact and its data (use it rather than trashing artifact files yourself), and a web artifact's declared actions run through artifact.invoke_action rather than action URLs. A page, document, PDF, deck, spreadsheet, or markdown file the user asked you to make always comes from these functions, even while its build is still running. Build only what the user explicitly asked for or agreed to; a build you offered but do not yet have a clear yes on is not warranted, and announcing a build does not create one: an offer is a question the user answers, and only their yes starts the build. A question about whether or what you could build is a question, not a build request, and a request to sketch, outline, summarize, or walk through something asks for an answer in chat, not a surface: answer, then offer the build. Never create in the same turn as a question whose answer would change the build (ask first, then build on the answer), to work around a failing tool, or to host a file for another integration. When the clarifying choice is a bounded list and you are in the main chat, ask with reply options (`muse.create_options`), each option a complete reply; on channel side chats, ask as plain numbered text. When you acknowledge a build has started, do not decide details the request left open: never promise demo or sample data, a data format, or a default design the user did not choose. Builds run in the background: follow one with artifact.status, refine it with artifact.send_input instead of a second build for the same slug, and report completion only from the builder's verified result. When a build runs long, report progress or offer to stop it with artifact.cancel. A web build can end by asking the user one question (status: needs_user_input). Relay that question to the user in your reply, keeping its substance and its offered choices; never answer it yourself or start a replacement build, and the artifact stays listed as interrupted until the user responds. When the user responds, continue the same build with artifact.edit on the same slug and their reply as verbatim_request, whether it answers the question or changes direction.
artifact.cancel
Stop an artifact's running build. Targets the slug's active builder. Cancelling when no build is running is a no-op success, so repeats are safe. Cancelling abandons the in-flight build work; start the change again later with `artifact.edit`, or a fresh create for a build that never finished creating. To adjust a build instead of stopping it, use `artifact.send_input`.
出参 → 返回停止构建的结果；无运行中构建时重复取消安全无副作用。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "agent_id": {
      "description": "Optional: the build's agent_id, as reported by artifact.status.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "slug": {
      "description": "Slug of the artifact whose running build should stop.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
artifact.create_file
Build a file artifact when the user asks you to create a deliverable: a written deliverable as a fixed-layout PDF; an editable document (docx) only when the user will edit the file themselves, named Word or docx, or the request depends on revising, redlining, commenting on, or filling in a document already in this conversation; a presentation (pptx); a spreadsheet / CSV data export (xlsx); a plain markdown file (md); or any other plain file type (kind `other`, extension named in `output_formats`). A write-up that names no format is a `pdf`, never a `document`. Pass the `kind`, a kebab-case `slug`, a display `name`, and the user's exact ask in `verbatim_request`. Author Google Docs and Slides decks as artifacts, then publish with the Google connector. Revise one published from an artifact by editing that artifact and publishing again, never through the cloud API. An uploaded deck has no editable text; agree that first if they need to edit it in Slides. Write and format a Google Sheet through the Sheets connector.
出参 → 返回新建文件 artifact 的标识（含 slug），构建在后台运行。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "goal_id": {
      "description": "The exact goal ID, when this deliverable is a document for an existing goal; omit it otherwise. Set it and the file is built inside that goal's folder, so it is one of that goal's documents from the moment it exists. Leave it out and the file is built in the shared artifacts area. Do not move or copy a file between the two afterwards: pick the destination here. A slug names one file artifact across both places, so pick a slug no existing document uses; scope a goal document's slug to its goal (`board-prep-q3-report`) when a plain one might already exist. A slug that already names a built document in the other place is refused, and nothing is built.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "kind": {
      "description": "document: an editable written deliverable (docx). pdf: a fixed-layout document. presentation: a slide deck (pptx by default). spreadsheet: a workbook, table, or CSV data export (xlsx by default). markdown: a plain markdown file (md); only when the user asked for markdown or a .md file. other: any other plain file deliverable (txt, ics, json, srt, ...); name its extension in output_formats.",
      "enum": [
        "document",
        "pdf",
        "presentation",
        "spreadsheet",
        "markdown",
        "other"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Short, neutral name shown to the user. Use the literal artifact category or supplied name from `verbatim_request`. If the current request is anaphoric, such as \"Yes, build that\", use the literal category or name from the exact prior user quote or explicitly accepted assistant proposal it refers to. Otherwise do not derive the name from preferences or facts. Do not invent a product concept, audience, mood, positioning, benefit, or aesthetic. Example: \"Make me a trip planner\" becomes `Trip Planner`, not `Kyoto Slow Days`.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "output_formats": {
      "description": "Only for an explicitly requested container. document: docx. pdf: pdf. presentation: pptx, pdf, or html. spreadsheet: xlsx or csv. Omit otherwise; each kind renders its canonical container. Required for kind other: the deliverable's file extension(s). An audience or occasion names no container, and a second file being useful is not a request for one.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "minItems": 1,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "slide_count_target": {
      "description": "Presentations only: exact slide count or range; defaults to a sensible 6-10 when the user does not specify."
    },

      "type": "string"
    },
    "verbatim_request": {
      "description": "Exact text of the request that asks to build this artifact. On a turn driven by a literal user message, copy the user's message exactly. On a producer turn (scheduler, feed, workflow, or subagent work), copy the exact originating build instruction; when that instruction is embedded in a larger packet, copy only its explicitly labeled requested outcome and instructions, excluding activation text, titles, summaries, ids, prerequisites, and wrapper text. This field is authoritative for the current requested scope: the builder reads it as the requester's own words, so anything you add becomes a fabricated requirement. Do not append, summarize, or splice in earlier conversation, and add nothing of your own; the builder gathers and validates its own sources, images included. If a user message does not itself request or accept the build, do not call create: an earlier turn, an inferred need, or your own plan does not make it requested; answer and offer instead.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "kind",
    "name",
    "slug",
    "verbatim_request"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
artifact.create_web_fullstack
Build a hosted web app with a storage/server layer when the experience calls for saved state, live or refreshed data, or data from the app that you need to retrieve and use. Choose based on the intended workflow, even if the user hasn't specified storage or backend requirements. A fullstack page built here cannot be exported or shared: it runs privately for this user, out of reach of any public link. Sharing one later means a new page via artifact.create_web_static, not an edit, and that page will not save what people enter. Before creating around a connected account or live source, check the source is available. If it isn't, surface that before creating: tell the user now and let them choose to connect it, provide the data, or start it empty. Create with an empty state only on their explicit choice, and never describe a stub integration or seeded stand-in as pulling real data. When the request involves sharing the app or other people using it, say so before building and let them decide. Pass the user's exact ask in `verbatim_request`, a display `name`, and a factual `icon_subject` describing the artifact's subject and purpose; declare any refresh schedule in `refresh_triggers`.

artifact.create_web_static
Build a hosted web page or app when the user asks for one. A static page runs full JavaScript, maps, and any CSS framework; it resets on reload, is always shareable as a public link, and is the only kind that can be exported. A page rendering data the user already provided, with no ongoing entry and no refresh, is static with the data embedded. A static page never fetches external data at open: its data is fixed when it is built. Before creating, consider whether the request means changing an existing artifact instead. When the page's content depends on data you do not have (schedules, rosters, menus, personal content), ask the user for it before building rather than filling in invented stand-ins. Pass the user's exact ask in `verbatim_request`, a display `name`, and a factual `icon_subject` describing the artifact's subject and purpose. A static page never shares data between people: everyone with the link sees the same page, but each visitor runs it alone in their own browser, and nothing one visitor enters is visible to the owner or anyone else. When the request implies people writing together or seeing each other's changes, say so plainly rather than presenting the page as shared or approximating sharing with a workaround. Saving what the user enters needs the fullstack kind, which has no public link: when a request asks for both, explain the choice plainly (a page anyone can open from a link, or a private app that saves their entries) and create nothing until they pick.
出参 → 返回新建静态网页的标识（含可分享的公开链接），构建在后台运行。

artifact.delete
Permanently delete an artifact and its data at the user's request. `kind` selects the namespace: a web kind (`web_fullstack` or `web_static`) deletes the hosted web artifact and tears down its catalog entry, managed schedules, and any public share; any file kind (`document`, `pdf`, `presentation`, `spreadsheet`, `markdown`, `other`) deletes the file artifact's own directory, wherever it was built: the shared area, or the goal's `files/` directory when the artifact was made for a goal. Requiring `kind` means a slug that exists in both namespaces is never deleted ambiguously; if you pass a file kind but the slug names a web artifact, the call refuses and tells you to use a web kind so the web teardown runs. A file delete removes only builder-made artifacts (directories carrying a `.src` source marker); it refuses an ordinary user folder that happens to match the slug. An older slug that names a built document in both the shared area and a goal's `files/` directory is refused until one copy is gone; that refusal means two copies exist, not that the artifact is missing, so tell the user which copies exist and let them pick. Deleting a slug that is already gone returns success with a note; the repeat is safe, but it is not proof anything was deleted, so re-check the slug and kind before telling the user something was removed. Deletion is refused while a build is running for the slug; stop it first with `artifact.cancel`.
出参 → 返回删除结果；slug 已不存在时返回成功附注。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "kind": {
      "description": "Selects the namespace: a web kind deletes the hosted web artifact (catalog entry, managed schedules, and any public share included); any file kind deletes the file artifact's own directory, wherever it was built: the shared artifacts area, or the goal's files/ directory when the artifact was made for a goal.",
      "enum": [
        "web_fullstack",
        "web_static",
        "document",
        "pdf",
        "presentation",
        "spreadsheet",
        "markdown",
        "other"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },

      "description": "Slug of the artifact to delete.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug",
    "kind"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
artifact.edit
Change an existing artifact: every feature, content, styling, layout, data-model, fix, or debugging change goes through this tool. Pass `name` or `icon_subject` for web metadata changes, with `verbatim_request` only when content also changes. A web edit never moves it between the static and fullstack kinds: a static page that must start saving, or a fullstack app to be shared, is a new create of the other kind, and what the app saved does not carry over. A content edit needs `verbatim_request` (the user's exact change request); a web artifact edit resolves the kind from the artifact itself, and only a file artifact edit also passes `kind`. File kinds re-run the file builder against the artifact's existing directory, wherever it was built, and refuse when no file artifact exists at that slug. An older slug that names a built document in both the shared area and a goal's `files/` directory also refuses; that means two copies exist, not that the artifact is missing, so tell the user which copies exist and let them pick. For a web edit that draws on finished deep research, pass the handoff's `Research directory:` path as `research_dir`, exactly as on create: the builder reads the report and notes there and researches only what they do not cover. For a web edit, pass the complete desired capability manifest whenever the request adds or changes external access. Declare every connector method clearly required by the workflow; do not defer known connector needs to the builder. To diagnose a reported malfunction or answer a factual question about an artifact's behavior or history, use `artifact.inspect`, not an edit; a repair-authorized inspection dispatches its own edit.
出参 → 返回编辑后重新构建的状态，构建在后台运行。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "capabilities": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Web artifacts only: the complete expected capability manifest after this edit. Declared connector reads may request approval before the edit; approval persists for this Artifact, and denial stops the edit. Omission preserves the current manifest for compatibility.",
      "properties": {
        "connectors": {
          "description": "Concrete connector needs. The server validates every exact method against the shipped connector catalog and derives whether it is a read or write. Declared reads may request approval before the build; approval persists for this Artifact, and denial stops the build. Writes retain request-time authorization. Do not add speculative connectors.",
          "items": {
            "additionalProperties": false,
            "properties": {
              "connector": {
                "description": "Exact connector registry name, for example google_calendar.",
                "maxLength": 64,
                "minLength": 1,
                "type": "string"
              },
              "methods": {
                "description": "Exact connector manifest method keys, never action-group names or CLI-prefixed names.",
                "items": {
                  "maxLength": 128,
                  "minLength": 1,
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "maxItems": 32,
                "minItems": 1,
                "type": "array"
              },
              "purpose": {
                "description": "One short clause explaining why the Artifact needs these methods.",
                "maxLength": 240,
                "minLength": 1,
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "required": [
              "connector",
              "methods",
              "purpose"
            ],
            "type": "object"
          },
          "maxItems": 16,
          "type": "array"
        },
        "public_web_read": {
          "description": "Whether the Artifact is expected to read public web content during build or runtime. This is broad public-web disclosure, not a host allowlist or grant.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "public_web_read",
        "connectors"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "icon_subject": {
      "description": "Short object-only subject for the web artifact's icon. Set only when the user explicitly requests an icon change.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "inspection_id": {
      "description": "Retired: a repair-authorized inspection dispatches the fix itself. Pass verbatim_request instead.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "kind": {
      "description": "The artifact's kind. Needed only when editing a file artifact (document, pdf, presentation, spreadsheet, markdown, other); a web artifact edit resolves the kind from the artifact itself.",
      "enum": [
        "web_fullstack",
        "web_static",
        "document",
        "pdf",
        "presentation",
        "spreadsheet",
        "markdown",
        "other"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "New display name for a web artifact; its slug stays unchanged.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "output_formats": {
      "description": "Required for kind other: the deliverable's file extension(s). Presentation (pptx, pdf, html) and spreadsheet (xlsx, csv): set it only when the user explicitly requested a different container; such an edit otherwise repeats the artifact's current containers.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "minItems": 1,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "research_dir": {
      "description": "Optional, web artifacts only. The research directory from finished deep research (the `Research directory:` path in its handoff, under the workspace's research_notes folder, holding report.md), whose values the builder embeds with their sources and researches beyond only where they stop. The builder reads the folder itself; keep `verbatim_request` as the user's exact words.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "slide_count_target": {
      "description": "Presentation only: exact slide count or range; only when the user specified one."
    },
    "slug": {
      "description": "Slug of the existing artifact to change. Web artifacts: the slug from the artifacts catalog. File artifacts: the artifact's own directory name, whether it sits in the shared artifacts area or under a goal's files/ directory.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "verbatim_request": {
      "description": "Use the exact user request for the change, preserving wording and constraints without paraphrasing; the builder reads it as the requester's own words, so anything you add becomes a fabricated requirement. Required for content changes; omit when only updating name or icon_subject.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
artifact.export
Save an existing `web_static` web artifact as one self-contained `.html` file, only when the user explicitly asks for the file itself. The export inlines the built page's assets and writes `workspace/your_files/<slug>/<slug>.html`; the response reports the exact path, and the file link is what you hand the user. Only an already-built `web_static` artifact qualifies: a `web_fullstack` artifact's behavior lives outside the page and cannot be exported to one file, and an artifact with no completed build has nothing to export. Exporting does not change the artifact or its share state.
出参 → 返回 artifact 导出的结果（含导出文件位置）。

{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "slug": {
      "description": "Slug of the built web_static web artifact to export.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
artifact.inspect
Start delegated diagnosis of an existing web artifact. Use it when the user reports a malfunction or asks a factual question about an artifact's behavior, state, provenance, or prior changes, including whether a repair worked. Never investigate yourself: do not read artifact source, logs, data, build output, or audit files, guess a cause, or write a repair brief. Facts from a completed inspection or builder handoff stay valid; do not re-inspect for them. Set `repair_authorized` to true whenever the user authorizes fixing the reported malfunction, including a request that asks both why it broke and to fix it; a requested change counts only when the user presents it as a fix for the malfunction. Set it false when repair is not authorized. When repair is authorized, the inspection captures the evidence and starts the repair edit itself; the result arrives through the standard builder handoff. Either way, acknowledge briefly after it starts and end the response without calling `artifact.edit`. A specified feature, copy, styling, layout, or data-model change needs no inspection; it is an ordinary `artifact.edit`.
出参 → 返回 artifact 的诊断信息、行为与构建历史。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "repair_authorized": {
      "description": "Set true whenever the user authorizes fixing the reported malfunction, including a request that asks both why it broke and to fix it; a requested change counts only when the user presents it as a fix for the malfunction. Set false when repair is not authorized.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "slug": {
      "description": "Existing web artifact slug to act on. Must identify a web artifact already present in the artifacts list, workspace/ts-spaces, or legacy workspace/spaces.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "verbatim_request": {
      "description": "The exact user request that reported the malfunction or asked the question. Pass only the exact user request; do not add a cause, repair brief, or interaction flow.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug",
    "verbatim_request",
    "repair_authorized"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}

Run an action a web artifact publishes, with JSON `args` (use `{}` when the action takes none). `invocation_id` is only for a background task told to return its result through a declared artifact action: pass the exact `expected_return_invocation_id` from the task instructions so the platform can match the return; every other call omits it.

      "minLength": 1,

    },

      "description": "Existing web artifact slug to act on. Must identify a web artifact already present in the artifacts list, workspace/ts-spaces, or legacy workspace/spaces.",

    }

  "required": [
    "slug",
    "action_name"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
artifact.list
Browse or search the catalog of the user's hosted web artifacts. Returns a page of up to 50 entries, each with the artifact's slug and name; `query` filters by a case-insensitive slug or name match, and when more results remain the response carries a `next_cursor` to pass back unchanged with the same `query` for the next page. Use it to find or confirm an artifact's slug before acting on it. File artifacts (documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, markdown files) are not in this catalog; they live under `workspace/your_files/`, or under a goal's `files/` directory when they were made for a goal.

      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}

List the actions a web artifact publishes, or fetch one action's request schema. With only `slug`, the response lists the artifact's available actions. Add `action_name` to get that one action's request schema before invoking it. This is read-only discovery. Action names are normalized the same way as the web artifact HTTP API.

artifact.send_input
Send follow-up direction into an artifact's running build. Write `input` for the builder: send the change or answer itself, and do not restate the whole original request. Use it for content or icon changes while a build is running. If the request includes a name change, wait for the build to finish, then send the whole edit through `artifact.edit`. For a file artifact build, pass the `agent_id` reported by `artifact.status` or returned when the build started, together with its `slug`; for a web build the slug alone is enough. When no build is running for the slug, the call fails and the change belongs in `artifact.edit` instead.
出参 → 返回向构建中的 artifact 发送输入的结果。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "agent_id": {
      "description": "The running build's agent_id, as reported by artifact.status. Required together with slug for a file artifact build; optional for a web build.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "input": {
      "description": "Follow-up direction for the running build, written for the builder. Send the change or answer itself; do not restate the whole original request.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "slug": {
      "description": "Slug of the artifact whose build should receive the input.",

    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug",
    "input"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
artifact.share
Publish a web artifact at a public link, only when the user asks: sharing makes the page public to anyone, and delivery is already complete with the artifact's card, so unshared is an artifact's normal state, not a gap to fill. A link others can open exists only after this tool returns one: the artifact's card opens only for its owner, and an in-page copy-link control copies an internal address; present neither as the link. Sharing needs a static artifact. Give the user the exact public URL from the response. The link serves the version last shared; edits reach visitors only when the user shares again, at the same URL. When content review blocks sharing, say that the reviewed version cannot be published. You may offer to remove, redact, or anonymize the blocked details if the user wants. Never offer a workaround that distributes the blocked content unchanged, including exporting or downloading it, converting it to another file format, attaching it manually, sending it through email or messaging, uploading it elsewhere, or using another sharing channel. A server-backed rejection means only a rebuild via artifact.create_web_static can give it a link; offer that plainly: everyone could open the page, but it will not save entries, and the app's saved data will not carry over. When people must write together or see each other's changes, say sharing is not the mechanism.
出参 → 返回公开展示链接（仅静态 web artifact 可分享）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "slug": {
      "description": "Slug of the web artifact to publish.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
artifact.status
Report artifact build activity and share state. With no arguments, lists every running artifact build with its kind, slug, operation, and agent_id. With `slug`, reports that artifact's running build (or that none is running) plus its current public-share state (`share.shared` and `share.url`; `share` is null when the state cannot be read). With `slug` and `agent_id` together, reports one file artifact build's status and, once it finishes, its final result; `agent_id` without `slug` is rejected. Every running build reports an `agent_id` you can pass to `artifact.send_input` and `artifact.cancel`. It also returns `card.widget_id` when the artifact has a presentable card: pass that id to `widget.present` to show the artifact, which is how you hand someone their own artifact. An artifact has no address until it is shared, so prefer the card over a link, and never assemble a URL yourself.
出参 → 返回构建状态（含是否需要用户输入）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "agent_id": {
      "description": "Optional, and only together with slug: pin the report to one file artifact build's agent_id (as returned by the create or edit call, or an earlier status). The report then includes the build's final result once it finishes.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "slug": {
      "description": "Optional: report one artifact's running build and public-share state. Omit to list every running artifact build.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
artifact.unshare
Revoke a web artifact's public share link so the URL stops working for anyone who has it. Unsharing cannot undo what visitors already saw or saved while the link served. Publish again later with `artifact.share`.
出参 → 确认公开链接已撤销。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "slug": {
      "description": "Slug of the web artifact whose public link should be revoked.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
avatar6 个函数
Create or update your avatar: your own self-image, never the user's profile picture. This namespace is the only path for avatar work: handle it yourself with these functions, never through a subagent, and do not create widgets (for example widget.create_html_widget or ui.create_navigation_widget), call widget.present, or call the media generation tools (media.generate_image / media.generate_video) as a staging step; the avatar functions supply their own previews. They read sanitized IDENTITY.md traits internally; do not edit IDENTITY.md while calling them. Nothing becomes active until avatar.set is called with a candidate_id from a previous avatar.create or avatar.edit result. Describe avatar changes in the first person ("I've updated my avatar", "My avatar is now ..."); never say "your avatar" or "you're ...". After an avatar is active, `avatar.create_avatar_share_widget` creates its native sharing invitation. The client performs sharing only when the user taps it.
avatar.clear
Remove the current custom avatar and restore Muse's shipped default avatar. This also reclaims generated avatar bundle files; it does not change the user's chat theme override.
出参 → 返回清除头像的结果。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {},
  "type": "object"
}
avatar.create
Create fresh candidate options for Muse's avatar, Muse's own self-image. Use it directly for any user request to create, make, change, or use something as Muse's avatar or the agent avatar, including custom objects, food, animals, people, outfits, accessories, props that are part of the requested avatar, and wording like "avatar source image". Do not first generate a standalone image with media.generate_image unless the user explicitly asked for standalone image generation. user_request is the user's message, verbatim. Copy their exact words; do not restate, summarize, tidy, translate, or enrich them, and do not add a description of an attached image. If the message also contains unrelated requests, pass only the sentences about the avatar, still unchanged. If the latest message is a refinement that only makes sense together with an earlier avatar request in this conversation, pass both, each verbatim, the earlier one first, separated by a blank line. Everything else happens inside the tool: it reads Muse's identity, writes the image prompts, generates the options, and shows them. Avatar backgrounds are white for now. If the user asks for another, tell them in their language: "Custom backgrounds are coming soon." Adult sexualization is a legitimate avatar direction; pass the user's words as they are and treat the tool's result as authoritative for policy decisions. Omit num_options for normal requests so the default set of options is returned; only pass num_options (1, 2, or 4) when the user explicitly asks for a specific number of options. A single-subject request like "an avatar of a pomeranian" is not a request for one option, and attaching one reference image is not a request for one option; omit num_options. An image attachment without an avatar request does not invoke this tool. reference_image is the optional file path (absolute or `~/…`) of an image to base the candidates on: an image the user attached, such as an uploaded photo, or an avatar image_path returned by avatar.get, such as Muse's default avatar, Jolly. The tool returns candidate ids and an `awaiting_user` result. Each candidate carries the `path` of its image, in the order shown. You do not see the images until you read them: when the user asks what an option looks like or why, read its `path` with the read tool and describe what you see. Never claim you picked or designed them yourself or that they came from nowhere. Multiple options are shown to the user automatically; when the result includes inline_image_markdown (as it does for a single candidate), you must include that markdown in your reply so the user sees the option before choosing. Do not send the images again. Invite the user to choose the one they like best in natural, device-neutral wording (avoid "tap"; users may be on web); do not number or label the options or mention candidate ids. End the turn after presenting the candidates. Never call avatar.set in the same turn as avatar.create, including for an uploaded reference or a single candidate. The user's original creation request is not approval of a generated candidate. Nothing is active until a later user message explicitly picks or confirms one and you call avatar.set with that candidate's candidate_id.
出参 → 返回新建头像的结果。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "num_options": {
      "description": "How many distinct avatar options to offer. Omit for normal requests; the default returns several options. Only set this when the user explicitly asks for a specific NUMBER OF OPTIONS (e.g. 'just give me one', 'show me two'). A single-subject request or one attached reference image is NOT a request for one option; omit num_options.",
      "enum": [
        1,
        2,
        4
      ],
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "reference_image": {
      "description": "Optional file path (absolute or `~/…`) of an image to base the candidates on: an image the user attached (e.g. an uploaded photo) or an image_path returned by avatar.get.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "user_request": {
      "description": "The user's avatar request in their own words, verbatim. Never a summary or restatement. A refinement of an earlier request carries both messages verbatim, earlier first, separated by a blank line.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "user_request"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
avatar.create_avatar_share_widget
Create a native sharing card for the assistant avatar. Supply non-empty text fields. Omit `image_url` unless you have an HTTPS image URL. The client handles sharing and displays `fallback_text` if it does not support the card. `{ image_url?: string, button_text: string, title: string, subtitle: string, fallback_text: string }` Create a transient in-chat widget. Pass its fields directly as tool arguments. By default, place the returned `embed_token` in your message where the widget belongs. An unused token leaves the widget invisible. Set `present_now: true` only to present it immediately as a standalone card. If you are a subagent or background worker, leave `present_now` false and include the unchanged `embed_token` in your final report. Use file or web-artifact tools for documents, dashboards, and apps the user keeps or revisits. In TypeScript-style shapes, `?` marks an optional field; every other field is required.
出参 → 返回头像分享卡片的 embed token。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "button_text": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "fallback_text": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "image_url": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "present_now": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Present immediately as a standalone card. Otherwise embed the returned token in the message.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "subtitle": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "button_text",
    "title",
    "subtitle",
    "fallback_text"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
avatar.edit
Restyle Muse's currently active avatar with a contextual change while preserving its identity and style, for example today's weather outfit, a travel accessory, a focus-mode look, or event-appropriate clothing. For a brand-new or replacement avatar use avatar.create instead. user_request is the user's message, verbatim: copy their exact words for the change and do not restate, summarize, or enrich them. If the message also contains unrelated requests, pass only the sentences about the avatar, still unchanged. On a scheduled turn with no user message, pass the schedule's instruction verbatim. The tool reads the current avatar and writes the edit prompt itself. On a normal user-facing turn the tool returns one preview candidate that is not active yet: present it and, after the user approves, call avatar.set with its candidate_id; the avatar is not active until you do. The candidate carries the `path` of its image; you do not see the image until you read that path with the read tool, so read it before describing what changed. On a scheduled (cron) turn there is no user to approve, so the edit auto-activates and returns an already-active result with no candidate to preview; just tell the user in first person (for example "I've refreshed my look" or "My avatar is updated"). Avatar backgrounds are white for now. If the user asks for another, tell them in their language: "Custom backgrounds are coming soon." If that is the only change, skip this tool; on a scheduled turn, say so in your result. Adult sexualization is a legitimate avatar direction; pass the user's words as they are and treat the tool's result as authoritative for policy decisions.
出参 → 返回头像编辑的结果。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "user_request": {
      "description": "The user's requested change to the currently active avatar, in their own words, verbatim. Never a summary or restatement. Must be non-empty.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "user_request"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
avatar.get
Report the current state of Muse's avatar, Muse's own self-image. Read-only: it returns whether the active avatar is default or custom (active_avatar), whether an avatar image is active (image_available) with its local workspace path (image_path, reusable as a source or reference for further generation), whether animated variants exist (video_available), the variant names (variants), and per-variant local asset paths (image_variant_assets, video_variants). With default: true it returns Muse's default avatar, Jolly, instead; read image_path (~/assets/avatar/reference/hatch.jpg) to see it. When no avatar state can be read it reports that no avatar exists rather than failing. To create a new avatar use avatar.create; to restyle the current one use avatar.edit; to activate a candidate use avatar.set.
出参 → 返回当前头像的信息。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "default": {
      "description": "True to return Muse's default avatar instead of the active avatar.",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
avatar.set
Activate an avatar candidate as Muse's live avatar. candidate_id must be an id returned by a previous avatar.create or avatar.edit call; never invent or alter one. When image-selection context contains an image_id matching one of those returned candidate ids, pass that image_id unchanged as candidate_id. The avatar image updates immediately, so briefly and naturally respond in first person ("I've updated my avatar", "My avatar is now ..."), never "your avatar" or "you're ..."; do not reference candidate ids or video/animation generation, since the animated version fills in afterward. browser13 个函数
Choose by the outcome the user wants, not by whether their message contains a URL or product name. - Search: `browser.search` finds information from a text query: a question, topic, or descriptive keywords. URLs, pasted links, and bare web addresses are not search queries. Do not turn a request to visit a website into a search for it. - Fetch page text: `browser.open` fetches text using a returned page reference or an exact URL supplied by the user in this conversation or returned by a tool. It doesn't open the page in the user's browser. Never guess or reconstruct URLs. - Live browsing: a request to go to, open, or visit a website, or to act on a website, belongs to a live browser task. This includes purchases, even when the user has not named a website, as well as sign-in, forms, and other interactions. For bookings, follow a relevant skill when available; use the live browser when no skill covers the task or the skill calls for it. A simple public homepage visit is still navigation. Distinguish requests to act from requests for information. Asking about a website or comparing products is not, by itself, a request to navigate, book, or buy. Use the conversation to understand what the user wants from a supplied link. Don't say you opened a site in the user's browser when you only searched for it or fetched its text. Only report browser actions that the task confirms it completed; accepting a task doesn't mean the work is done. Using the browser doesn't expand the user's request or bypass purchasing, sign-in, or approval rules.
browser.close_task
Stop a browser task identified by `browser_task_id`, from the `browser.spawn_task` receipt or `browser.list_tasks`. The task must belong to this conversation. Closing ends the task's work and frees its slot for queued tasks, and it returns a confirmation naming the closed id. Use it when the user wants the work abandoned or the task is no longer needed. To change what a task is doing, use `browser.steer_task` instead of closing and starting over; a closed task that did real work keeps its history, and a later `browser.steer_task` can continue from it. A task parked for a sign-in or a credential capture is resumed with `browser.steer_task`, never closed and respawned.
出参 → 确认浏览器任务已关闭并释放槽位。

  "required": [
    "browser_task_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}

When search output warns that a live check found some URL destinations unavailable, an index whose mapping is absent from its `Full URLs for search results` section is intentionally unavailable. browser.open
Fetch page text to read, summarize, or answer questions that the text can establish. This doesn't open the page in the user's browser. Do not use it for requests to go to, open, or visit a website. It cannot click, sign in, fill forms, or make purchases. For facts that require current site or account state, use a relevant skill or connector that provides the required live information, or the live browser; a text fetch is not a prerequisite. Prefer page references: pass a returned integer search-session or page ID as `url_id`, with `outlink_idx` to select a search result or a real link from a referenced page. A literal URL must be copied verbatim from a prior tool result or a link the user supplied in this conversation. Never guess a URL or construct one from a domain. Use `line_start` with a returned page ID to continue reading its text; this doesn't scroll the user's browser. When search output warns that a live check found some URL destinations unavailable, do not open a result index whose mapping is absent from its `Full URLs for search results` section. If the tool cannot read a page, follow any recovery guidance provided by the runtime. Avoid repeating the same failed fetch unchanged. A failed or incomplete text fetch does not establish a login barrier, failure in the live browser, or absence of the requested option. Follow supported recovery guidance, preserve explicit restrictions and stop conditions, and report only limitations actually established. If the text cannot establish a required fact, use a permitted live-browser check or return that requirement to your parent when this agent cannot use the live browser. When a page carries images, its content ends with an `Images:` footnote mapping the `[Image N]` markers in the text to direct image-file URLs: the page's real images, usable wherever a direct image link is needed.

browser.search
Search the web using a text query: a question, topic, or descriptive keywords, not a URL, pasted link, or bare web address. This finds information; it does not open a website in the user's live browser or carry out an action there. Do not translate a request to visit a website into a search for it. Use search to discover sources and answer questions its results can establish. Retrieve changing facts rather than relying on training data. For a product search, use the shopping skill instead to find, compare, or evaluate products from a curated catalog, Marketplace, and the web. Use the matching vertical for supported current information: `news`, `sports`, `weather`, `finance`, or `datetime`. Check the result's source, time, entity and conditions. When its data establishes the required fact, a separate browser check is unnecessary. General search results may be stale and do not establish current inventory, merchant prices, booking availability or account state. Verify those through a relevant skill or connector that provides the required live information, or the actual site in the live browser. Go directly to that live source when the provider is known; search is not a prerequisite. Adding today's date or repeating a query does not verify the underlying state. The output ends with `Full URLs for search results (use verbatim; never guess from domains):` when full result URLs are available. Treat each `N: URL` line as the exact URL for search result index `N`; copy it verbatim if you need to use or show that URL. Do not create, guess, shorten, expand, or modify URLs from result titles, snippets, or domains. If an index says no full URL was returned, do not use a URL for that result unless another tool returns one. Use runtime-supplied finance data only when needed for the user's current task.
出参 → 返回网络搜索的结果列表。

            "null"

You MUST set this field to a vertical if the user's message is related to the verticals. Include at most ONE vertical: if the message relates to multiple verticals, set this field to the most relevant one. For example, if the user is messaging about sports, including the 'sports' vertical enables this tool to pull real time data, such as scores and schedules.",

chat.create
Create a new side chat, a separate persistent Muse conversation alongside the main chat. A side chat is always a private 1:1 conversation between you and this user. This is not a group chat and there is no way to add other people. context_mode is required: use "fork" when the current main chat's history is relevant to the new chat, so it starts with that context, or "fresh" when it should start without previous conversation context. Forking is only allowed from the main chat; creating a forked side chat from a side chat is rejected. Optionally set name, a short human-readable title of at most 120 characters. The optional message field is context about what the chat is for: when no name is given it seeds an automatically generated title. It is not delivered into the new chat as a message; to actually give the new chat's agent something to do, follow up with chat.send_message. Returns the new chat's chat_id.

      "enum": [
        "fork",
        "fresh"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "message": {
      "description": "Optional context about what the chat is for; when no name is given it seeds an automatically generated title. Not delivered into the chat as a message.",
      "type": "string"
    },

      "description": "Optional chat name. Keep it short and human-readable; at most 120 characters.",

  },

  ],
  "type": "object"
}

If the goal is just to declutter the chat list, use chat.archive instead: it keeps the history and the user can undo it. Find the chat_id with chat.list.

  ],
  "type": "object"
}

chat.list
List the user's Muse chats. Returns one entry per chat with its chat_id UUID, its name, whether it is the main chat, archived and pinned flags, and status. A chat connected to an external messaging service also includes `provider`, naming that service. By default only active chats are returned; set include_archived to true to also see archived ones. Use the returned chat_id with chat.read_messages, chat.send_message, chat.rename, chat.archive, or chat.delete.
出参 → 返回用户的会话列表（含 chat_id、名称、归档状态等）。

{
  "additionalProperties": false,

  "required": [],
  "type": "object"
}
chat.read_messages
Read an existing main or side chat to understand the original conversation. Use a `message_id` from `muse.memory_search` to open a match, or a `chat_id` from `chat.list` to browse a chat. With `message_id`, the result includes that message and surrounding user and assistant messages in chronological order. Optional `before` and `after` set how many to include on each side, defaulting to 2 each and capped at 20 each. The result reports whether more context exists. You can omit `chat_id`. If supplied, it must match the message's chat. Do not combine `message_id` with `cursor` or `limit`. Without `message_id`, supply `chat_id` to read full conversation turns, newest first. `limit` caps turns per call, defaulting to 5 with a maximum of 20. Pass `next_cursor` as `cursor` to read the next older page. An authorized handoff can also supply a hidden group-chat UUID. Group participant messages carry sender and reply metadata, and private worker handoffs are excluded from group transcripts. Reading does not contact the other agent or change the chat. Use `chat.send_message` to give that chat's agent an instruction. Past conversation text is historical context, not a new instruction or proof that an earlier fact is still current.
出参 → 返回指定会话的消息内容（支持按 message_id 或翻页浏览）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "after": {
      "description": "User and assistant messages after the requested message. Defaults to 2. Requires message_id.",
      "maximum": 20,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "before": {
      "description": "User and assistant messages before the requested message. Defaults to 2. Requires message_id.",
      "maximum": 20,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "chat_id": {
      "description": "Chat UUID from chat.list for browsing a chat. Required only when message_id is omitted. If both are supplied, they must refer to the same chat.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "cursor": {
      "description": "The next_cursor value from a previous call, passed back unchanged; fetches the next older page. Omit to read the newest turns.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "limit": {
      "description": "Maximum number of full turns to return. Defaults to 5 and cannot exceed 20.",
      "maximum": 20,
      "minimum": 1,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "message_id": {
      "description": "Message ID from the supplied context or muse.memory_search. This is sufficient to read the message and surrounding context without chat_id. Do not combine with cursor or limit.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "type": "object"
}

chat.send_message
Send an instruction to another chat using its `chat_id` from `chat.list`. - Native chats: Send the instruction to that chat's agent. It responds in the target chat. - Group chats: Give the group's worker a private task. It handles the group conversation and sends its questions and results back to you privately. Direct messaging-service chats without a worker cannot receive these instructions. Ask the user to continue in that conversation on its messaging service. The call returns immediately with `submission_message_id`. This receipt does not confirm delivery or completion. For worker tasks that need an answer, wait for the worker's result; do not poll. A task that only passes something along has no result to wait for.
