permissions1 个函数
Tool namespace `permissions`.
permissions.list_pending
List permission requests currently waiting for the user, including what each action is for and what access it would grant. Use this when the user asks what pending permissions are or why they are being requested. This is read-only. Results are newest first, include the request time in UTC, and contain at most 20 pending permission requests per page so a large queue stays manageable. `remaining_count` reports how many older requests remain. When `next_cursor` is present, call again with that exact value as `cursor` to inspect the next older requests. Use `approval_id` to correlate a tool failure or background result with the exact pending request, then use its returned purpose and scope to explain the block. A card may remain pending for future work after a caller's wait expired; its presence does not mean that invocation is still running or that its action ran. An absent ID does not prove approval or denial. IDs convey no decision authority. `attention_mode: background` means the request came from work that does not block the active chat. Treat the returned fields as factual grounding, not a response template. Answer naturally and do not mechanically restate every field. State returned facts directly and confidently. Use relevant conversation history, scheduled tasks, goals, or saved memory only to make the explanation more useful, not as proof of where the request came from. State or imply that a specific conversation, task, goal, or memory caused the request only when the returned fields explicitly establish that connection. process7 个函数
Remove a finished exec background session from tracking and discard its buffered output. Fails while the process is still running; stop it first with process.kill.
process.clear
Remove a finished background process session from tracking and discard its buffered output. Only sessions that already exited can be cleared: the call fails if the process is still running (stop it first with process.kill) or the session id is unknown. After clearing, the session no longer appears in process.list and its logs are gone. Clearing is optional housekeeping; finished sessions otherwise stay listed with their output available to process.log.
出参 → 返回清理已结束后台会话的结果。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "properties": {
    "session_id": {
      "description": "The session id exec returned for this tracked command.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "session_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
process.kill
Terminate a background process session started by exec. The kill tears down the whole process tree, including descendants that detached from the original process group, then reports the session's final status, exit code and signal, and failure kind. Killing does not remove the session: its output stays readable with process.log until you drop it with process.clear. Fails if the session id is unknown. Backgrounded commands that finish on their own report back automatically; kill is for stopping work you no longer want.
出参 → 返回终止进程的结果（含退出码与信号）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "properties": {
    "session_id": {
      "description": "The session id exec returned for this tracked command.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "session_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
process.list
List every background process session the current agent has started through exec, running or finished. Takes no parameters. Each entry reports the session id, command line, pid, working directory, status (running, completed, or failed), exit code and signal, failure kind, whether the command was backgrounded, elapsed milliseconds, total output characters, whether output was truncated, and whether the session runs in a PTY. Sessions are scoped to the calling agent; other agents' commands do not appear. Backgrounded exec commands deliver their terminal result into your context automatically, so do not use this tool to wait for completion. For one session's output use process.log or process.poll.
出参 → 返回本 agent 的后台进程会话列表。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "properties": {},
  "required": [],
  "type": "object"
}
process.log
Read a paged window of the accumulated output of a background process session started by exec. Output is split into lines: offset is the zero-based line to start from (default 0) and limit is how many lines to return (default 200, maximum 1000). The reply carries the requested lines plus nextOffset and totalLines for paging, the session status, exit code and signal, failure kind, whether output was truncated, and a tail excerpt. Reading is non-destructive and repeatable: unlike process.poll it consumes nothing, so you can page through history freely. Use process.poll instead when you want to wait briefly for fresh output.
出参 → 返回进程累积输出的分页内容。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "description": "Maximum number of lines to return. Default 200, clamped to 1-1000.",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "offset": {
      "description": "Zero-based line offset into the session's accumulated output. Defaults to 0.",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "session_id": {
      "description": "The session id exec returned for this tracked command.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "session_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
process.poll
Wait up to timeout milliseconds for a background process session started by exec to produce new output or exit, then return its state. The reply carries the session status, exit code and signal, failure kind, the stdout and stderr produced since the last poll (deltas are consumed and returned once), elapsed milliseconds, total output characters, whether output was truncated, and a tail excerpt of recent output. timeout defaults to 1000 and is clamped to 0-120000; 0 returns the current state immediately. Backgrounded exec commands deliver their terminal result into your context automatically, so never poll just to wait for completion; if a finished session's completion message is already queued for automatic delivery, this call returns an error instead of double-reporting it. For the full accumulated log use process.log; to stop the process use process.kill.
出参 → 返回等待后的进程新输出增量与状态。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "properties": {
    "session_id": {
      "description": "The session id exec returned for this tracked command.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "timeout": {
      "description": "How long to wait in milliseconds for new output or exit before returning. Default 1000, clamped to 0-120000; 0 returns immediately.",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "session_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
process.send_keys
Send named key presses to a background process session started by exec, encoded as terminal control sequences and written to the session's input. Intended for PTY sessions running interactive programs. keys is an ordered list of case-insensitive tokens: enter or return, tab, escape or esc, space, backspace, up, down, left, right, home, end, pageup, pagedown, insert, delete, f1 through f12, and control chords written c-<char> (for example c-c, c-d, c-z). An unsupported token fails the whole call and nothing is sent. Set eof true to close the session's input after the keys. The reply reports the session id, bytes written, and whether input was closed. For plain text use process.write; to see the program's response, follow with process.poll.
出参 → 返回按键发送的结果（写入字节数等）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "properties": {
    "eof": {
      "description": "Close the session's input after sending the keys. Defaults to false.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "keys": {
      "description": "Ordered key tokens to send, for example [\"c-c\"] or [\"escape\", \"enter\"]. The tool description lists every supported token.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "session_id": {
      "description": "The session id exec returned for this tracked command.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "session_id",
    "keys"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
process.write
Write raw text to the stdin of a background process session started by exec. data is sent exactly as given, so include a trailing newline to submit a line to line-oriented programs. Set eof true to close the session's stdin after the write, which lets programs that read until end-of-input proceed. The reply reports the session id, bytes written, and whether stdin was closed. Fails if the session is unknown or its stdin is no longer writable. For named terminal keys such as enter, arrows, or control chords in a PTY session, use process.send_keys; to read what the program printed back, follow with process.poll.
出参 → 返回向进程 stdin 写入的结果。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "properties": {
    "data": {
      "description": "Raw text to write to the session's stdin, sent exactly as given. Include a trailing newline to submit a line.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "eof": {
      "description": "Close the session's stdin after this write. Defaults to false.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "session_id": {
      "description": "The session id exec returned for this tracked command.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "session_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}

shopping.create_shopping_results_widget
Present shopping product cards from resolved catalog, Marketplace, connector, or browser results. This tool presents the widget immediately as a standalone card. Subagents and background workers cannot call it; report the content back instead. In TypeScript-style shapes, `?` marks an optional field; every other field is required. Use the artifact returned by `shopping.resolve_results`. Preserve the returned URLs, product references, provider identity, retailer context, and advertised actions; follow the owning connector skill for provider-specific workflows. Pass exactly one of `path` or `products`; prefer `path` when another tool wrote a `kind: "shopping_results"` JSON file. `{ path?: string, products?: { url: string, name: string, citation_id: string, image_url?: string | null, type?: "catalog" | "marketplace" | "browser", product_id?: string, provider?: string, brand?: string, price?: string, sale_price?: string, retailer_name?: string, primary_action?: "add_to_cart" }[] }` `provider` is the owning connector skill's canonical identifier, independent of the rendering type. Connector cards use `type: "browser"`. The server adds trusted provider attribution when all products share a provider, and a retailer subtitle when they also share a non-empty `retailer_name`; do not supply logos or attribution yourself. `brand` identifies the product brand. Advertise `primary_action: "add_to_cart"` only when that connector skill supports the operation. It requires `type: "browser"`, `provider`, and a non-empty `product_id` unique within the widget. `retailer_name` is optional context as required by the connector. Keep both agentic checkout capability flags false. A click queues a normal agent turn requesting one additional unit; it does not mean the cart changed or authorize checkout. social1 个函数
Search Instagram, Threads, and Facebook by topic, including the user's own posts and activity. For Instagram, Facebook, and Threads links, use the respective CLIs directly. Fall back to `social.search` or browser if the CLI results are insufficient. When using this tool for a specific post, set `post_url` to its exact link instead of translating the link into a query. For a structured read of a specific account, use that service's skill (facebook_cli, instagram, threads) instead. Pair with `browser.search` when a question also spans the open web. On infrastructure errors, fall back to browser.search rather than retrying.
social.search
Search content across Instagram, Threads, and Facebook, including the user's own posts and activity. Use it for free-text topic search and for direct lookup of an exact social-post URL. For Instagram, Facebook, and Threads links, use the respective CLIs directly. Fall back to `social.search` or browser if the CLI results are insufficient. When using this tool for a specific post, set `post_url` to its exact link instead of translating the link into a query. For a structured read of a specific account, use that service's skill (facebook_cli, instagram, threads) instead. Pair with `browser.search` when answering broader questions. If this tool returns an infrastructure error (for example, connector not registered), fall back to `browser.search` rather than retrying. Bold key entities and cite diverse sources when presenting results. Results come back with the writing system you searched in first. A post the platform marked as written in a different script is listed below a marked line rather than removed, and the counts are reported beside the results. The line sorts by writing system, not by language, so a post in the same script as your query but another language sits above it. Write the query in the language the answer should be sourced in, which is normally the language the user is writing to you in. Prefer the posts above the line: a source the user cannot read is one they cannot check. Reach below it only when the answer lives nowhere else. Whichever side it sat on, say which language a source is in whenever that is not the language the user is writing to you in.
出参 → 返回 Instagram / Threads / Facebook 的内容搜索结果。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "properties": {
    "authors": {
      "description": "Hard-filter to posts authored BY specific people. Only set this when the user's intent is to see content that person created or shared - NOT content about them from others.\n\nUSE authors when the user wants content FROM/BY someone.\n\nUse \"@self\" when the user refers to their own content.\n\nDO NOT use authors for public figures when the user wants content ABOUT them (news, discussions, mentions by others). Instead, include the person's name in semantic_queries.\n\nThis distinction matters for public figures because there is a lot of content about them from other accounts. Constraining to authors would miss news coverage, fan posts, and commentary.\n\nFor friends and non-public figures, always use authors - third-party content about them is rare, so the user almost certainly wants their posts directly. When the user identifies someone by a social relationship (\"my friend\", \"someone I follow\"), also set relation_to_author:\n- \"what's up with my friend [friend_name]\" becomes authors: [\"[friend_name]\"] with relation_to_author: \"friend\".\n- \"what's my friend [friend_name] up to\" becomes authors: [\"[friend_name]\"] with relation_to_author: \"friend\".\n- \"anything new from [name]\" becomes authors: [\"[name]\"].\n\nPrefix handles with @ (\"@zuck\", \"@selenagomez\"). For public figures and well-known accounts, prefer the @handle when you know it confidently, even if the user said the display name (\"Mark Zuckerberg\" becomes \"@zuck\"). Use one entry per person, not both. Fall back to the display name only when you don't know the handle. Partial names are fine.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "content_type": {
      "description": "Content type filter.\n\nSet ONLY when the user constrains the format to images or videos, either explicitly or implicitly:\n- \"video\", \"reel\", \"clip\", and \"vid\" all mean \"video\".\n- \"photo\", \"pic\", \"image\", and \"screenshot\" all mean \"image\".\n\nIf the user does not specify content type, OMIT this field and return all content types.",
      "enum": [
        "image",
        "video"
      ]
    },
    "group_names": {
      "description": "Filter to posts from specific Facebook Groups by name.\n\nSet when the user asks about content from one or more Facebook Groups. Each entry should be the group's display name as it appears on Facebook (e.g., [\"Instant Pot Community\", \"Dog Lovers\"]).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "key_celebrities": {
      "description": "Key people the query is about.\n\nUse key_celebrities when a notable person is the SUBJECT of the query — it boosts their authored posts in ranking without filtering to them.\n\nDo NOT remove the person's name from semantic_queries when key_celebrities is set — the name helps surface content about them.\n\nFormat: display name (Mark Zuckerberg) unless @handle is provided (@zuck).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "languages": {
      "description": "The languages the answer should be sourced in, as ISO 639-1 codes (\"ko\", \"ja\", \"es\").\n\nThis steers retrieval, so it changes which posts come back rather than only how they are ordered. Results are otherwise ranked with the writing system you wrote the queries in first, and posts in other scripts are listed below a marked line.\n\nSet this when the user is asking about a language other than the one they are writing to you in: \"what are Korean fans saying about the finale\" asked in English needs `[\"ko\"]`. Without it those answers may not come back at all, and any that do sort to the bottom.\n\nLeave it unset for an ordinary question. Do not set it to the language the user already writing in, and do not list extra languages hoping for more results: each one you add promotes that language's posts, and a source the user cannot read is one they cannot check.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "location": {
      "description": "The location filter for a geographic search: a city name, an address, or a landmark.\n\nThe backend will geocode this to latitude/longitude coordinates and filter posts to those geotagged within a default radius (50km).\n\nSet when the user's query has a geographic intent.\n\n## Be as specific as possible\nAlways include state/province and country when applicable to avoid ambiguity.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "platform": {
      "description": "Set ONLY if the user explicitly applies a platform constraint:\n- Explicitly, such as \"on Instagram\", \"from Facebook\", \"in Threads\", or \"IG only\".\n- Implicitly via platform references or shortnames in the request, such as \"IG\", \"Insta\", \"FB\", \"on my Instagram feed\", or \"Threads post\".\n\nIf the user does not imply a platform, OMIT this field and search all platforms.",
      "enum": [
        "facebook",
        "instagram",
        "threads"
      ]
    },
    "post_url": {
      "description": "Direct lookup for one exact Instagram, Facebook, or Threads post URL, including `threads.com/@user/post/...`, `threads.com/t/...`, `threads.net/@user/post/...`, and `threads.net/t/...` short links.\n\nSet this when the user provides a specific post link and wants information about that exact post. Use `post_url` instead of translating the link into `semantic_queries`, and instead of opening the link in the browser.\n\nDo not combine `post_url` with other fields.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "ranking_intent": {
      "description": "Determines how search results are ranked.\n\n- \"informational\" is the default (applied when omitted), and retrieves the most accurate results. For how-to, advice, tutorials, factual questions, reviews, comparisons, \"best X\", recipes, recommendations.\n- \"engagement\" retrieves posts that have high engagement and are popular. For trending topics, opinions, \"what are people saying\", viral content, hot takes, debates, memes, reactions, community discussion, celebrity/gossip.\n- \"recency\" progressively downranks older posts within relevance ranking (posts within 48 hours keep full weight; older tiers sink, down to 70% past three months). ONLY for time-critical breaking updates (live scores, \"just happened\", official announcements). Do not use this for general news queries — pair \"informational\" with `since` instead.",
      "enum": [
        "informational",
        "engagement",
        "recency"
      ]
    },
    "relation_to_author": {
      "default": "all",
      "description": "Filter by author's social relationship. Can be used with or without `semantic_queries`.\n\n- \"friend\" - Mutual connections (IG mutual follows + FB friends). Trigger: \"my friends\".\n- \"followee\" - People you follow. Trigger: \"people I follow\", \"accounts I follow\".\n- \"follower\" - People who follow you. Trigger: \"my followers\".\n- \"all\" - Default. Omit for default behavior.\n\nSet whenever user mentions a social relationship. For pure browse with no topic, set this WITHOUT semantic_queries. For topical queries, set this WITH semantic_queries.",
      "enum": [
        "all",
        "friend",
        "followee",
        "follower"
      ]
    },
    "semantic_queries": {
      "description": "Search queries. The FIRST element is your primary query, used for ranking: a concise, specific phrase (3-8 words) capturing the core intent. Include key entities and proper nouns; prefer concrete terms (\"Taylor Swift Eras Tour\", not \"popular concert tours\").\n\nProvide 2-4 additional queries targeting different facets of the topic. Each must retrieve a substantially different set of posts — no near-duplicate rephrasings. Break the topic into subtopics, stakeholders, or content types. Results from all queries are merged and ranked, with the first query boosted.\n\nDo NOT duplicate values you are already passing in other fields: a name you put in `authors` (a hard FROM-filter), group names, platform names, temporal words, and content format words all belong to their own fields (authors, group_names, platform, since, content_type), and repeating them in queries hurts retrieval. The one deliberate exception: when a person is the query's SUBJECT, their name STAYS in the query (add them to key_celebrities as well — that field only boosts ranking; the query is what retrieves content about them).\n\nOmit this field entirely when there is no specific search topic (\"what are my friends up to\"); never fill it with generic terms like \"recent posts\".",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "since": {
      "description": "Filter to posts POSTED on or after this date: YYYY-MM-DD. Always past dates, never future; this filters when content was posted, not when events will occur.\n\nSet for recency-sensitive queries, with the lookback matched to intent:\n- breaking/trending → days\n- news/updates → weeks\n- seasonal/holiday → months\n- time-bounded (\"Q4 2023\", \"during [event]\") → set both since and until\n\nOmit for evergreen how-to questions.\n\nWhen since is set, remove temporal words (today, recently, latest, trending, this week, breaking, current) from semantic_queries entirely — date filtering is handled by this field.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "top": {
      "description": "How many results the call returns (best-effort). Results from every semantic query are merged and ranked, and the summary carries the top N of that merged set, not N per query. Default 6; the maximum is 25 (higher values are clamped).\n\nRaise it when a broad sweep genuinely needs more breadth than the default; leave it unset for a focused lookup.",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "until": {
      "description": "Only return posts created on or before this date: YYYY-MM-DD. Always past dates, never future; this filters when content was posted, not when events will occur.\n\nSet this only for historical date ranges (\"Q4 2023\", \"during Connect 2022\").\n\nWhen until is set, remove temporal words (today, recently, latest, this week, current) from semantic_queries entirely — date filtering is handled by this field.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
subagent5 个函数
Stop a child agent by id when its work is no longer needed or it is stuck. To redirect a struggling agent instead, use subagent.send; to find ids and check state first, use subagent.list.
subagent.close
Stop one of your child agents by id and end its work. Use this when the delegated work is no longer needed, the agent is stuck, or it should not keep going. To redirect an agent instead of stopping it, use `subagent.send`; to find the right id and check state first, use `subagent.list`. Closing a browser task owner stops the whole browser task: the response then includes its `browser_task_id`, and next time its parent agent can close that task through the dedicated browser-task control. If a browser task owner has no task id on record, the error explains how the parent agent can find and close the task there.
出参 → 返回关闭子代理的结果（browser 任务会附带 browser_task_id）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{

    "id": {
      "description": "Target agent id (from subagent.spawn or subagent.list output).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "scope": {
      "description": "Where the target may live: 'direct' (default) covers your immediate children, 'descendants' the full subtree under you.",
      "enum": [
        "direct",
        "descendants"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
subagent.list
List your child agents (in main chat, also other chats' and scheduled jobs' agents), grouped into active and recent, with a normalized status (running, done, interrupted, failed), task and final response previews, timing, and whether a finished result was already seen. Running entries include how long the agent has been running and how long since its last activity. A quiet agent is not proof it is stuck; it may be inside one long tool call. Entries carry the agent ids the other subagent tools need, plus the browser task id for browser task owners and the artifact slug for artifact builders. In main chat each entry's `owner` says whether a chat or a scheduled job owns it, with the schedule and run ids for scheduled work, so a scheduled job's agents are never mistaken for missing. You can view agents owned by another chat or a scheduled job but not steer or stop them here; manage scheduled work with the cron tools. Check status only to act on it: the user asks where things stand, you need an agent id, or you suspect slow or failed work. Finished results are delivered to you automatically; mentioning running work unprompted needs no fresh check, and calling this in a polling loop wastes turns.
出参 → 返回子代理的状态列表（含预览与计时）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "description": "Max entries to return. Default 20, max 200.",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "scope": {
      "description": "'direct' (default): your immediate children. 'descendants': the full subtree of agents under you.",
      "enum": [
        "direct",
        "descendants"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "type": "object"
}
subagent.resume
Resume one of your interrupted child agents by id so it continues its existing task from where it stopped. Only a paused or interrupted agent can be resumed. An agent that already finished or shut down is not resumed; the call returns an error saying so, because resuming a terminal agent re-runs nothing. Spawn a new agent with `subagent.spawn` to continue that work. Resume restarts the agent on its own task; to give it new direction once it is running again, use `subagent.send`. Two kinds of agents refuse generic resume: browser task owners continue through their parent agent's dedicated browser-task control, and a web artifact builder whose build is still in flight cannot be resumed; wait for it to finish or send it guidance with `subagent.send`.
出参 → 返回恢复中断子代理的结果。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{

      "type": "string"
    },
    "scope": {
      "description": "Where the target may live: 'direct' (default) covers your immediate children, 'descendants' the full subtree under you.",
      "enum": [
        "direct",
        "descendants"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
subagent.send
Deliver follow-up input to one of your running child agents by id. Delivery is ASYNC: a success response means the message was submitted, not applied. The instruction stays pending until the agent's handoff or completion result reports it, so do not describe it as done, do not poll for it, and do not fabricate the outcome. Handle anything else the turn needs, then end your response. Provide the input in `message`, or in `items` for images or files; `items` takes precedence when both are set. Set `interrupt` true to cut off the agent's current work first, so the new input starts a fresh turn instead of queueing behind the old one. Browser task owners cannot be steered by agent id; their parent agent must use the dedicated browser-task control with its `browser_task_id` instead. To start ordinary delegated work when no suitable agent exists, use `subagent.spawn`.
出参 → 返回消息已提交（异步投递，不代表已执行）。

subagent.spawn
Delegate a task to a new child agent that works on it in the background while you continue. Do not spawn a generic child for requested website navigation, purchases, or other live-browser work: logged-in sites, clicking, forms, or multi-step interactions. That work belongs to the browser-task delegation route, not another generic child. Generic subagents may search the public web and fetch page text from links supplied by the user or returned by tools; requests to visit or interact with websites are returned to the parent for appropriate delegation. This call is ASYNC: the response only confirms the spawn and returns the new agent id. Results arrive later through the runtime, so never treat the response as completion and never produce results for delegated work yourself. After spawning, acknowledge what you delegated and end your response; do not poll, sleep, or promise a delivery time. Spawn all independent agents at once instead of one at a time. Provide the task in `message`, or in `items` when it needs images or files; `items` takes precedence when both are set. Manage the agent afterwards by its id: `subagent.list` shows status, `subagent.send` delivers follow-up input, `subagent.resume` restarts an interrupted one, and `subagent.close` stops one. Some work has its own dedicated parent-agent capability and cannot be spawned here, including browser tasks, artifacts (a page, app, document, deck, or spreadsheet), and accepted Idea builds. Artifacts do not need a subagent: the artifact tools already run the build in the background and report back. If the user asks for a subagent, tell the child to use the artifact tools instead of creating a file itself. A rejected spawn returns a structured error with a stable reason code; fix the cause it names instead of retrying the same call.
出参 → 返回新子代理的 agent id；结果稍后由 runtime 自动送达。

            "type": "string"

  ],
  "type": "object"

todo1 个函数
Records the full working todo list for this conversation. Use it for several steps or requests that need to stay in view. Keep one item `in_progress` while you can work, and mark work `blocked` when progress depends on new input or a result.
todo.write
Records your working todo list for the current task, replacing the previous list. Use it for a task with three or more distinct steps, or when several requests need to stay in view. Skip it for a quick answer or a single action. Always send the full list, with at most 25 items, and preserve item text when updating its status. Keep one item `in_progress` while you can work and leave work you have not started `pending`. Continue actionable work until it is complete or genuinely blocked. Keep only unfinished and blocked work. Before ending your turn, remove completed and cancelled items, including work you just finished and verified. You can report those results after updating the list. Send an empty list when nothing remains. Mark an item `blocked` when progress depends on new input or a result. While you are waiting for a running agent or background result, mark the affected items `blocked`. Resume them when the result arrives. Mark dependent work `blocked` too if it cannot advance on its own. Before ending your turn, explain each new blocker, what would unblock it and how the user can help if needed. Continue independent work. Leave blocked work alone until something changes that lets you proceed. Do not use `blocked` for work you can still advance.
出参 → 返回更新后的任务清单。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "todos": {
      "description": "The complete todo list; this call replaces the previous list.",
      "items": {
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "status": {
            "description": "Use `pending` for work not started, `in_progress` for the one active item, `blocked` when progress depends on new input or a result, `completed` when the outcome is established, and `cancelled` when it no longer applies.",
            "enum": [
              "pending",
              "in_progress",
              "blocked",
              "completed",
              "cancelled"
            ],
            "type": "string"
          },
          "text": {
            "description": "One concrete step, phrased as an action.",
            "type": "string"
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "text",
          "status"
        ],
        "type": "object"
      },
      "maxItems": 25,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "todos"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
tool_search1 个函数
Load all function schemas for one or more deferred tool namespaces before calling their functions for the first time.
tool_search.load_tool_namespace
Load all function descriptions and parameter schemas for one or more tool namespaces. Use when a namespace or one of its functions is marked deferred and its full interface is not already in context. Call this with the namespace names in `paths` and it returns the full function interfaces, after which those functions are callable normally. A namespace counts as loaded while the full interfaces from its load are still in your context: call its functions directly rather than loading it again. Functions whose full schemas are provided up front are already callable without loading. This tool is only for the tool namespaces listed in the tool list: that list is the complete loadable set, so never attempt to load a name that is not on it. Skills are not tool namespaces — capabilities from connected accounts and apps (email, calendar, retailer accounts, music, and similar) are skills; discover those with muse.skill_search, never with this tool.
出参 → 返回所加载命名空间的完整函数描述与参数 schema。

  "type": "object"
}
tracking10 个函数
Track concrete plans, commitments, and outcomes the user cares about beyond the immediate conversation, including reservations, deliveries, reminders, trips, and ongoing projects. Do not require an explicit request to track them or a minimum amount of work. Keep the item open while the relevant event, delivery, or follow-up is still pending, even if booking or checkout is complete. Skip ordinary conversation and requests whose outcome is fully resolved in the current turn. Associate the work with its existing goal or tracked item before scheduling a call, cron, heartbeat check, or other background mechanism. Close a reminder once delivered and nothing remains owed. When work belongs to an existing tracked item, associate it with that item. When the user explicitly restarts a completed responsibility, reopen that existing item with set_status; never create a replacement instance. Create a new tracked item only when no existing record represents the responsibility - and an active user goal is such a record: never create a tracked item, subgoal, or any second goal record to represent check-ins, accountability, or monitoring for a user goal that exists. Attach the cron or check-in to that goal (cron owner `goal:<goal-slug>`) and log progress in the user_goal namespace. Close tracked items proactively when the best available evidence shows the responsibility ended; do not wait for the user. Use conversation history, goal state, completed work or tool results, reliable real-world facts, and current time relative to known dates. Respect an explicit stop immediately. Examples: delivery received; event ended; target reached; window expired; user cancelled. Silence or one finished step alone is not enough. Call `tracking.set_status` with `completed` in the same turn when that evidence arrives. An activity entry or a refreshed pulse does not close the item. Close it even when its activity log already records the outcome. Use the list, search, and get functions to resolve identity before creating or updating. Search matches terms across ids, titles, `current_state`, and descriptions and returns lifecycle state and timestamps. Every set_status call requires a concise user-facing `reason` explaining the transition. Each tracked item has a workspace at `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/`; read its `GOAL.md` first before doing anything related to the item. Documents the user asked for go in `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/files/`, which the user sees as the item's documents; check logs, watermarks, snapshots, and other bookkeeping go in `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/hidden_files/`, which the user does not see. Do not add unrequested files under `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/files/` or `workspace/your_files/`: a check-in records its outcome with `create_entry`, not as a new document.
tracking.create
Create a tracked item for a concrete plan, commitment, or outcome the user cares about beyond the immediate conversation, such as a reservation, delivery, reminder, trip, or ongoing project. Track it even when the user does not say "track this" or the next step is quick. Keep it open while the relevant event, delivery, or follow-up is still pending, even if booking or checkout is complete. Skip ordinary conversation and requests whose outcome is fully resolved in the current turn. Associate the work with its tracked item before scheduling a call, cron, heartbeat check, or other background mechanism. For a user-requested reminder, record the scheduled time as when the user is due and close the item once the reminder is delivered and nothing remains owed. Before creating, resolve identity with `tracking.list` or `tracking.search`: when the work belongs to an existing tracked item, log to that item with `tracking.create_entry` instead, and when the user explicitly restarts a completed responsibility, reopen that item with `tracking.set_status`; never create a replacement instance. An active user goal is such an existing record: when the work serves one of the user's existing goals (accountability, check-ins, nudges, monitoring, or reminders for that goal's outcome), it belongs on that goal as goal-owned schedules and timeline entries, never as a new tracked item, subgoal, or second goal record shadowing the goal. Attach the cron or check-in to that goal (cron owner `goal:<goal-slug>`) and log progress with `user_goal.create_entry`. Give the item a `title` that is a concise noun phrase naming the work itself, a one-line `current_state` pulse, and a two or three sentence `description`; detailed progress belongs in activity entries, not the description. Optionally nest it under a top-level tracked item with `parent_goal_id`, and classify it with `goal_kind` and `value_alignment`. Creation returns the new item immediately, including its `goal_id`. Each created item gets a workspace at `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/` with a `GOAL.md`; read that file before doing later work on the item.
出参 → 返回新建跟踪项（含 goal_id 与工作区路径）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "current_state": {
      "description": "The one-line user-facing state. Write one short pulse from the newest evidence that states the single most useful current or forward-looking status: a result, progress marker, specific wait, blocker, monitored condition, or scheduled event. Do not claim work is currently in progress, append a generic next step, or restate the title or description.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "description": {
      "description": "Two or three natural, user-facing sentences that explain the tracked work at a high level. Put detailed progress and state changes in activity entries instead.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "emoji": {
      "description": "Single emoji for the item. Defaults to a generic goal emoji when omitted.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "goal_kind": {
      "description": "outcome = result to achieve. behavior = action pattern to adopt. learning = skill to acquire. habit = recurring practice. maintenance = hold a standard. recovery = return from a setback. identity = who the user wants to become. exploratory = open-ended discovery.",
      "enum": [
        "outcome",
        "behavior",
        "learning",
        "habit",
        "maintenance",
        "recovery",
        "identity",
        "exploratory"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "parent_goal_id": {
      "description": "Id of an existing TOP-LEVEL tracked item to nest this one under. The parent must itself be assistant-tracked work, not a user goal.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "title": {
      "description": "Concise user-facing noun phrase naming the tracked work itself, not an instruction. Avoid generic leading verbs like `Track ...`; use concrete domain wording (`Wimbledon daily analysis`, `Childcare coordination`). Current activity and status go in current_state.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "value_alignment": {
      "description": "Short user-facing note on why this work matters to the user.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "title",
    "current_state",
    "description"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
tracking.create_entry
Add one activity entry to a tracked item's timeline. Log activity incrementally whenever anything happens on tracked work, including a step starting or completing, a check, new or confirmed information, deliverable progress, an artifact change, a result, checkpoint, check-in, feedback, direction change, blocker, schedule change, or lifecycle change. Do not wait for a milestone or material change. Keep the entry concise and user-facing, say what happened and any result, and record each activity once. The runtime reads each new entry and replaces the item's `current_state` pulse when the activity supports a newer or more useful current or forward-looking status, and otherwise preserves it; it also refreshes the item's attention state. Do not make a separate `tracking.update` call for that state decision. An entry on a nested item is also rolled up onto its parent's timeline automatically. Use `effective_at` when logging something that happened earlier than now; it accepts RFC 3339 timestamps or `YYYY-MM-DD` and defaults to now. An entry does not change lifecycle status. When the whole tracked responsibility has ended, close the item with `tracking.set_status` in the same turn. Find the item's `goal_id` with `tracking.list` or `tracking.search`, or create the item first with `tracking.create`.
出参 → 返回新增的时间线条目。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "current_state": {
      "description": "State the activity's main outcome in one line.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "description": {
      "description": "One concise, human-friendly sentence about what happened and, when applicable, what the result was.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "effective_at": {
      "description": "When the activity actually happened. Accepts RFC 3339 timestamps or YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to now.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "goal_id": {
      "description": "Tracked item id, as returned by tracking.list, tracking.search, or tracking.create.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "title": {
      "description": "Concise user-facing title for this activity entry.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "goal_id",
    "title",
    "current_state",
    "description"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
tracking.delete
Permanently delete a tracked work item by `goal_id`, removing it and its activity timeline from the tracked-work roster. Files from the item's `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/` directory are preserved on disk, and the response lists the preserved paths. Deleting is for mistakes and for items the user explicitly asks to remove. When the responsibility simply ended (shipped, event over, target reached, window expired, user cancelled), close it with `tracking.set_status` completed instead so the record and its history stay available. To remove a single wrong timeline entry rather than the whole item, use `tracking.delete_entry`.
出参 → 返回删除结果（磁盘文件保留并列出路径）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "goal_id": {
      "description": "Tracked item id to delete permanently. Tracked item id, as returned by tracking.list, tracking.search, or tracking.create.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "goal_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
tracking.delete_entry
Delete one activity entry from a tracked item's timeline by its `update_id` (from the timeline `tracking.get` returns). The response confirms the deleted entry's id, its item's `goal_id`, and its title. This removes only the single entry; the tracked item itself and the rest of its history stay. To fix a wrong entry instead of removing it, use `tracking.update_entry`. To remove the whole item use `tracking.delete`, and to close finished work use `tracking.set_status`.
出参 → 返回被删除条目的确认信息。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "update_id": {
      "description": "Activity entry id, from the timeline tracking.get returns.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "update_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
tracking.get
Read one tracked work item in full by its `goal_id`. Returns the item's metadata (title, `current_state` pulse, description, lifecycle status, parent linkage) together with its complete activity timeline, plus any pending suggestions, associations, and recent briefings. Each timeline entry carries its `update_id`, title, outcome line, description, and effective time; those `update_id` values are what `tracking.update_entry` and `tracking.delete_entry` take. Each tracked item also has a workspace directory at `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/`; read its `GOAL.md` before doing any substantial work related to the item. When you do not know the `goal_id`, find it with `tracking.list` or `tracking.search` first.
出参 → 返回跟踪项的完整信息与活动时间线。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "goal_id": {
      "description": "Exact tracked item id to read. Tracked item id, as returned by tracking.list, tracking.search, or tracking.create.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "goal_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
tracking.list
List the work items you are tracking for the user. Returns up to `limit` items (default 100) with each item's id, title, `current_state` (the one-line status pulse), description, lifecycle status, timestamps, and parent linkage, plus any storage warnings. Items here are assistant-tracked responsibilities: monitoring, follow-ups, background work, and other work you carry across turns on the user's behalf. The user's own goals are a separate surface and never appear here. Use it to resolve identity before mutating: check whether a responsibility already has a tracked item before creating one with `tracking.create`, and confirm the exact `goal_id` before calling `tracking.update`, `tracking.set_status`, or `tracking.create_entry`. For a keyword lookup across a long roster use `tracking.search`; for one item's full timeline use `tracking.get`.
出参 → 返回跟踪中的事项列表。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "description": "Maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.",
      "maximum": 100,
      "minimum": 1,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "offset": {

tracking.search
Search your tracked work items with keyword terms. Terms match case-insensitively against each item's id, title, `current_state`, and description; words shorter than two characters are ignored, and the query must contain at least one term of two or more characters. Matches cover every lifecycle state, so completed items are found too. Results are ranked by how many terms match, then by most recent update, and return compact projections (long text fields are cut at 2,000 characters) with lifecycle status, timestamps, and parent linkage, plus the total match count. Returns at most `limit` matches (default 10, maximum 100). Use it to resolve whether a responsibility already has a tracked item before creating a new one with `tracking.create`, and to find ids for `tracking.get`, `tracking.update`, or `tracking.set_status`. For a plain bounded roster with full text use `tracking.list` instead.
出参 → 返回关键词匹配的跟踪项。

  "properties": {

      "description": "Maximum matches to return. Defaults to 10.",
      "maximum": 100,
      "minimum": 1,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "query": {
      "description": "Terms to match against tracked item id, title, current_state, and description. Words shorter than two characters are ignored; at least one longer term is required.",
      "minLength": 2,
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "query"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
tracking.set_status
Set a tracked work item's lifecycle to active or completed, with a required user-facing `reason` explaining the transition. This is the complete lifecycle: active means the responsibility remains open, completed means it ended. Close tracked items proactively when the best available evidence shows the responsibility ended; do not wait for the user. Use conversation history, completed work or tool results, reliable real-world facts, and current time relative to known dates. Respect an explicit stop immediately. Examples: delivery received; event ended; target reached; window expired; user cancelled. Silence or one finished step alone is not enough. Use active only to reopen the existing completed item when the user explicitly restarts the responsibility; never create a replacement item with `tracking.create`. The change runs through the daemon's tracking lifecycle coordinator, which may also record a closing or reopening activity entry; the response says whether anything changed and includes any recorded entry. Find the `goal_id` with `tracking.list` or `tracking.search`.
出参 → 返回状态变更结果（active/completed）。

{

  "properties": {
    "goal_id": {
      "description": "Tracked item id, as returned by tracking.list, tracking.search, or tracking.create.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "reason": {
      "description": "Concise user-facing explanation of why the lifecycle changed. Required.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "status": {
      "description": "The complete lifecycle for tracked work: active means the responsibility remains open, completed means it ended.",
      "enum": [
        "active",
        "completed"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "goal_id",
    "status",
    "reason"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
tracking.update
Patch a tracked work item's metadata by `goal_id`: title, `current_state`, description, parent linkage, `goal_kind`, or `value_alignment`. Only the fields you pass change. Use it only for an explicit correction that is not already represented by new activity: when something happened, log it with `tracking.create_entry` instead, and the runtime refreshes the item's `current_state` pulse from that entry on its own. Do not make an update call solely to restate progress or append a generic next step. Lifecycle is not editable here; open or complete the item with `tracking.set_status`. `parent_goal_id` moves the item under a new parent, which must be a top-level tracked item; pass an empty string to detach the item to top-level. The target must be an assistant-tracked item; this tool cannot edit the user's own goals. Find the exact `goal_id` with `tracking.list` or `tracking.search`. `escalation` is what to do if a stated condition is not met by a date: `{condition, due_at, action}` with `action` `notify` (tell the user) or `ask` (the user must decide next). Set it only from something the user said, a conditional follow-up or a hard deadline with a consequence they named, and only after they confirm it; pass `null` to clear one they have withdrawn. trash3 个函数
List Muse trash entries with their trash_id, status, expiry date, original path, and top-level contents. Read-only. Use it to find the trash_id an entry needs for trash.restore.
trash.list
List every entry in Muse's recoverable trash. Read-only and takes no parameters. Returns a markdown table sorted newest first with each entry's trash_id, status (active, restored, or expired), expiry date, original path, and top-level contents. Only entries with status active can still be restored: a restored entry keeps its metadata as an audit record, and an expired entry's content has already been removed. Active content stays inspectable under `~/.local/share/Trash/hatch/<trash_id>/files/` until it expires, 30 days after trashing. Use this to find the trash_id that trash.restore needs, or to confirm what an earlier trash.put captured. To trash something use trash.put; to recover an entry use trash.restore.
出参 → 返回回收站条目列表（markdown 表格）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {},
  "required": [],
  "type": "object"
}
trash.put
Move one file or directory into Muse's recoverable trash and get back a trash_id for later recovery. Use this instead of permanent deletion (such as rm through exec) whenever removing user files should be reversible: workspace cleanup, replacing an old version, or any destructive file-removal flow. The path resolves against the agent home directory; the entry must exist, and a trailing symlink is trashed as the symlink itself, never followed to its target. The move is a rename into `~/.local/share/Trash/hatch/<trash_id>/files/`, so the source must live on the same filesystem as the home directory, and the trash directory itself is refused. The result reports the trash_id, the original path, the trashed location, and the expiry date. Entries are cleaned up automatically 30 days after trashing; until then the trashed content stays inspectable under `~/.local/share/Trash/hatch/<trash_id>/files/`. To review what is in the trash use trash.list; to bring an entry back use trash.restore.
出参 → 返回 trash_id、原路径与过期时间。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "description": "File or directory to move into recoverable trash. Relative paths resolve against the agent home directory. The entry must exist; a trailing symlink is trashed as the symlink itself, not its target.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
trash.restore
Move an active trash entry back out of Muse's recoverable trash. trash_id is the id returned by trash.put or shown by trash.list; only an entry with status active can be restored, and a restored or expired entry fails with an error. By default the entry returns to the original path recorded when it was trashed; pass custom_path to restore it somewhere else. Both destinations resolve against the agent home directory, and missing parent directories are created as needed. Restore never overwrites an existing path: if the destination is already occupied the call fails, so inspect the occupant, pick a new name or directory, and call again with custom_path. On success the result reports the trash_id, the original path, and the restored path, and the entry's metadata stays behind as an audit record. To find an entry's id first use trash.list; to trash something use trash.put.
出参 → 返回恢复结果（原路径与实际恢复路径）。
入参 schema（点击展开） 
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "custom_path": {
      "description": "Optional destination path; resolves against the agent home directory. If omitted or blank, the entry is restored to its recorded original path. Restore never overwrites an existing path; on a conflict, retry with a new name or directory here.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "trash_id": {
      "description": "Trash id returned by trash.put or shown by trash.list. Only an entry with status active can be restored.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "trash_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}

ui.create_navigation_widget

Durable goals the user is working toward. Create a goal when the user is working toward an enduring outcome, behavior, or area of life. Recognize durable goals even when the user never says "goal": repeated aspirations, progress updates, setbacks, commitments with a timeframe, or asking for help with a whole area of life. Not goals: fleeting todos, one-time reminders, minor updates that belong on an existing goal, or work you carry for the user (that is the tracking namespace). Clarify one question at a time (use `muse.create_options` for a bounded choice; do not list options in prose). Clarify the outcome the user wants when it is unclear. Offer practical help. Raise a goal only when relevant to the current conversation, and log milestone wins that same turn without derailing the topic. Use the list, search, and get functions to resolve goal identity before creating or updating. Search matches terms across goal ids, titles, `current_state`, and descriptions and returns lifecycle state and timestamps. Every set_status call requires a concise user-facing `reason` explaining the transition. Proactive Letters delivered in chat are produced from these goals; when the user asks to stop them, set `pushable: false` on that goal with `user_goal.update` (that goal's Letters still appear in the Goals tab). Each existing goal has a workspace at `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/`; before updating or helping with an existing goal, read its `GOAL.md` first. `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` is your own notes on the goal rather than a document for the user. Write in `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` where the goal stands now, the user's constraints on the goal such as schedule, injuries, budget, or boundaries, the facts you learned while setting the goal up, and the current shape of the plan. Update `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` with the file tools when you finish setting a goal up, when a constraint or the plan changes, and when helping with the goal reveals information worth keeping. When a goal is created, the runtime seeds `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` with a header carrying the goal's title, id, slug, and description. The runtime does not write to `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` again. All of `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` is yours to edit, the seeded header included. Renaming or recategorizing a goal updates the goal record but not `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md`, so the seeded header can go stale. When the seeded header and the goal record disagree, trust the goal record from `user_goal.get`. The goal record carries the category, so confirm with `user_goal.get` before concluding a goal has none. When the record's own category is absent, read `/opt/hatch/skills/goals/SKILL.md` alone.

user_goal.create_entry
Add one activity entry to a user goal's timeline. Log an entry when the user reports progress, a result, a setback, a milestone, or a decision that moves or changes the goal; log milestone wins the same turn they happen without derailing the conversation. Keep the entry concise and user-facing, say what happened and any result, and record each activity once. The runtime reads each new entry and replaces the goal's `current_state` pulse when the activity supports a newer or more useful current or forward-looking status, and otherwise preserves it. Do not make a separate `user_goal.update` call for that state decision. An entry on a nested goal is also rolled up onto its parent goal's timeline automatically. Use `effective_at` when logging something that happened earlier than now; it accepts RFC 3339 timestamps or YYYY-MM-DD and defaults to now. Find the goal's `goal_id` with `user_goal.list` or `user_goal.search`, or create the goal first with `user_goal.create`.

A goal the user finished, achieved, or abandoned should instead be completed with `user_goal.set_status`, which keeps its history visible. user_goal.list

user_goal.search
Search the user's goals with keyword terms. Terms match case-insensitively against each goal's id, title, `current_state`, and description, across every lifecycle state including completed goals. Results are ranked by how many terms match, then by most recent update, and come back as compact projections with lifecycle status, category (`null` for an uncategorized record), and timestamps plus a total `match_count`. The `query` needs at least one term of two or more characters; `limit` defaults to 10 (maximum 100). Prefer this over `user_goal.list` when the roster is long and you are hunting for one specific goal, including checking whether a past or completed goal already covers what the user just described. voice4 个函数
End the caller's live voice conversation with Muse whenever they indicate they want to stop talking, including casual goodbyes, on turns spoken in that call; separate from outbound phone calls Muse places on their behalf.
voice.end_call
End the caller's current live voice conversation with Muse when they indicate they want to end the conversation, including casual goodbyes. It works only on turns spoken in a live voice call; on other turns, including typed ones, reply to a goodbye normally. This tool cannot place, manage, or end outbound phone calls Muse places to other people or businesses; use the phone tools for those calls. Pause ongoing work to call this tool without waiting for the task or its results, unless the caller explicitly asks you to finish something before hanging up. Do not send a goodbye or narrate ending the call. After success, continue unfinished requests unless the caller also cancelled them; you may send a normal response when the task completes. This tool takes no arguments and does not speak a goodbye. It returns an error if ending the call is unavailable.

voice.set
Set the user's preferred voice. Pass the exact voice id or voice display name from the user's request, a recent voice result, or a server-authored picker/listing; the runtime resolves names only when they identify one catalog voice or one validated saved voice with exactly one profile. A saved-voice listing may instead provide the opaque saved_voice_id and profile_id pair. The runtime never trusts caller-supplied profile text. A successful call persists the selection immediately. Confirm the selected voice naturally without claiming exactly when the audio transport applies it. The current tool catalog is authoritative: when this tool is present, never refuse a new voice-selection request merely because an earlier conversation turn or memory says voice switching failed or was unavailable. Call the tool once and base the response on its current result.

widget7 个函数
These rules cover `widget.create_list_widget`, `widget.create_map_widget`, `widget.create_html_widget`, and `widget.create_html_file_widget`. `widget.create_letter_widget` always presents directly and returns no token. Create a transient in-chat widget. Pass its fields directly as tool arguments. By default, place the returned `embed_token` in your message where the widget belongs. An unused token leaves the widget invisible. Set `present_now: true` only to present it immediately as a standalone card. If you are a subagent or background worker, leave `present_now` false and include the unchanged `embed_token` in your final report. Use file or web-artifact tools for documents, dashboards, and apps the user keeps or revisits. In TypeScript-style shapes, `?` marks an optional field; every other field is required. ## HTML widget authoring These rules govern `widget.create_html_widget` and `widget.create_html_file_widget`. Follow every rule here whenever you write or edit widget HTML. ### Fragment shape - For `html`, pass only the compact fragment rendered inside the existing iframe shell. Do not paste complete document HTML into `html`; omit `<!DOCTYPE>`, `<html>`, `<head>`, and `<body>` wrappers. - Set `box-sizing: border-box` and wrap or constrain content so the widget never overflows the chat at any width. - Use text labels or inline `currentColor` SVG/CSS marks for icons; do not use emoji as UI icons or decoration. - Do not reference `sandbox://...` URLs or guessed internal raw-file routes such as `/fs/raw/...` or `/media/raw/...` from widget HTML. In-page anchors such as `#details` are fine. - A remote image in widget HTML must be a stable public URL: never a signed or expiring CDN link (Instagram/`cdninstagram`, presigned S3, tokened URLs), which dies when the widget replays from history. With no stable URL, drop the image rather than hotlink an expiring one. - Widget HTML is stored whole and replayed with the chat history, so it must stay small: 1 MB is the hard limit, and the tool rejects anything larger, both inline `html` and `html_file`. Never inline audio, video, or other media as base64 data URLs; only a tiny image or icon may ride inline as a data URL. For voice notes, recordings, or any real media file, do not use a widget at all: return the media file as an own-line sandbox link instead. ### Fallback text - Include `fallback_text` whenever the widget has meaningful visual or interactive content. `fallback_text` is a concise plain-text fallback for the widget (at most 120 characters), such as `Solar System`, `Vendor Comparison`, or `Mortgage Calculator`. - Do not render `fallback_text` inside the HTML as a heading, caption, title, or visible label just because the field exists. It is used outside the widget when the HTML cannot render and in compact surfaces such as quoted reply previews. ### Widget state - Keep interactive widget state in the backend bridge, not browser storage. Call `window.hatchWidget.getState(defaults)` with the complete initial state; when no durable state exists, the bridge seeds and persists those defaults. Treat the returned object as the complete application state, replace it after every user mutation with `window.hatchWidget.setState(nextState)`, and re-render when the `hatch-widget-state` event supplies newer `event.detail.state`. Treat that object as the single source of truth for dynamic content such as checklist rows; do not keep the only copy in a JavaScript closure. - Do not use `<form>` elements or form submission for widget interactions. Use buttons, inputs, and explicit event handlers that update the complete state through `window.hatchWidget.setState(nextState)`; the bridge, not browser form behavior, owns persistence. - Never use `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, or IndexedDB for widget state. Those stores are iframe/WebView-local and are not the durable Muse widget state bridge. ### Theming The `html` fragment MUST be theme-aware: it renders on both light and dark app backgrounds, so a light-only palette looks broken in dark mode. The shell sets `html[data-theme="light"]` or `html[data-theme="dark"]` and exposes inherited neutral-UI variables. Use each variable only for its semantic role: - `--hatch-widget-bg` is the outer background and may be transparent. - `--hatch-widget-surface` is a standard card or control background. - `--hatch-widget-surface-muted` is a lower-emphasis background. - `--hatch-widget-text` is primary foreground text or icons. - `--hatch-widget-muted` is secondary foreground text or icons. - `--hatch-widget-border` is for borders and dividers. - `--hatch-widget-accent` is for accent text, icons, borders, and indicators. - `--hatch-widget-on-accent` is the foreground for a filled accent surface. - `--hatch-widget-focus` is for focus rings. - `--hatch-widget-shadow` is for box shadows. Never use `--hatch-widget-bg`, `--hatch-widget-surface`, or `--hatch-widget-surface-muted` as a `color`; pair neutral backgrounds with `--hatch-widget-text` or `--hatch-widget-muted`. For example, a neutral button can pair `background: var(--hatch-widget-surface)` with `color: var(--hatch-widget-text)` and a `--hatch-widget-border` border. Use `--hatch-widget-accent` as a foreground or border by default. If an intentional filled accent surface is necessary, pair it with `--hatch-widget-on-accent`, which is supplied for that purpose and has at least 4.5:1 contrast in both themes. Drive all neutral UI from these variables (or from your own variables redefined under `html[data-theme="dark"]`); do not hard-code white/near-white backgrounds or black/gray text for neutral UI. ### html_file paths - Pass a path to a local `.html` or `.htm` file. Relative paths are resolved from the home directory; `workspace/...`, `/workspace/...`, `~/...`, `file://...`, and `sandbox://workspace/...` are supported. - Files over 1 MB are rejected. If your file is over the limit, that almost always means media was inlined as base64; remove the media and share it as a sandbox file link instead of shrinking or splitting the encoding. - Do not pass paths under `workspace/your_files/` or `workspace/visual_grounding/`; those are generated artifacts and must be returned as own-line preview links instead of rendered with `html_file`.

Create an in-chat HTML widget from a local HTML file. Read HTML from a local `.html` or `.htm` file. Relative paths resolve from the home directory; `workspace/...`, `/workspace/...`, `~/...`, `file://...`, and `sandbox://workspace/...` work. Files over 1 MB are rejected: widgets are compact UI, not media containers. Never pass paths under `workspace/your_files/` or `workspace/visual_grounding/`; return those as own-line preview links instead. widget.create_list_widget
Create a native list card of skill-directed results, links, flights, calendar entries, or email entries. Use native list cards for skill-directed results such as flights and fitness classes. Use 1–20 rows. Non-flight rows require non-empty titles. Copy image URLs from source results when available. Use `type: "link"` with an HTTP(S) `data.url` for a row that opens a URL and `type: "send_message"` for a row the user taps to send `data.text` as their reply; calendar and email rows select a glyph only. Omit `type` for a generic row. File rows are unsupported. If the active client cannot render list cards, present the results as Markdown instead. For a link list, pass arguments like this: ```json { "title": "Results", "items": [ { "title": "Result name", "type": "link", "data": { "url": "https://example.com/result" } } ] } ``` Include `items` in the tool arguments. Add an optional list `title` and `subtitle`; omit `title` for a list without a heading. For a flight list whose action is not booking, add one list-level `flight_action` object with a short single-line `cta_text` and `response_message_prefix`. The runtime appends the selected itinerary and total to that prefix. For example: ```json { "flight_action": { "cta_text": "Add to plan", "response_message_prefix": "Add this flight to my trip plan:" } } ``` Omit `flight_action` for the default `Book with <agent_name>` action. Use one action for the whole flight list; do not put action copy in individual rows. Choose action copy appropriate to the current flow, and make `response_message_prefix` describe the same intended action as `cta_text`. For non-flight rows, add optional string fields `subtitle`, `tertiary_title` and `image_url`, or an `icons` array of image URL strings. Set row `type` to "generic", "link", "send_message", "calendar", "email", or "flight". Use `type: "send_message"` with a non-empty `data.text` string only for rows that offer the user a reply to choose. Use link or generic rows for results. Keep the text aligned with the row's title and subtitle, with no hidden instructions. Creating the widget sends nothing. Copy any supplied `image_url` unchanged and never invent one. For flights, set row `type` to "flight". Supply either inline `data.flight_data` or `data.flight_details_file` with a JSON file path. Create one row per complete trip, including every slice and connection. Omit `data.slice_index` and row presentation strings. When flight results are already JSON, save the unchanged search output to a temporary file and pass its path in `data.flight_details_file`. Select one object with `data.json_pointer`, an RFC 6901 pointer such as "/offers/0". Omit the pointer when the whole file is one flight object. Inspect the file to choose result indexes. Do not rewrite or trim its flight objects, or copy them into tool arguments. Keep the file until widget creation succeeds. The runtime loads each file once per list and stores the selected data. File paths and pointers are not stored or sent to clients. For example, put this row in the list's `items` array: ```json { "type": "flight", "data": { "flight_details_file": "/tmp/flight-search.json", "json_pointer": "/offers/0" } } ``` Select one complete flight object from the file, using either the inline schema below or the normalized search schema. For normalized search data, the runtime maps segment `departing_at` and `arriving_at` to the widget's local datetimes and derives display fields. It preserves the other offer facts. Do not add a separate offer id to file input. Use a different JSON pointer for each selected result. For browser results, supply inline `data.flight_data` or save the same object to a file. Populate it from verified source facts. Preserve known baggage, fare conditions, passenger cabins, and durations. Include source summary facts when detailed passenger facts are unavailable. Omit unknown optional facts. Use a stable private-mapping key for `id` if the source has no offer id. Do not combine inline and file input in one row. Check the source flight facts before presenting. Present each result set once, using either `present_now` or the returned embed token. Do not present a second copy solely to correct cosmetic details. After presenting, add useful recommendations or caveats without repeating the flight inventory in prose. Use this JSON shape for an inline flight row. Replace the illustrative values with source facts and omit optional fields that the source does not provide. Put each row inside the list's `items` array. For file input, save only the object inside `data.flight_data`, or use `json_pointer` to select that object within a larger document. ```json { "type": "flight", "data": { "flight_data": { "id": "offer_id_from_source", "passengers": [ { "type": "adult" }, { "age": 8 } ], "expires_at": "2026-09-14T18:00:00Z", "price": "567.00", "currency": "USD", "airline": "Example Airlines", "duration": "2h20m", "slices": [ { "duration": "2h20m", "fare_brand": "Business Flex", "segments": [ { "from": "SFO", "to": "PDX", "depart": "2026-09-15T07:35:00", "arrive": "2026-09-15T09:55:00", "flight": "EX24", "carrier": "Example Airlines", "operating_carrier": "Example Regional", "operating_flight": "ER24", "duration": "2h20m", "passengers": [ { "cabin": "Business", "bags": { "carry_on": 1, "checked": 2 } }, { "cabin": "Business", "bags": { "carry_on": 1, "checked": 2 } } ], "carrier_code": "EX" } ] } ], "refundable": "yes", "changeable": "yes", "refund_penalty": "200.00 USD", "change_penalty": "100.00 USD", "refund_penalty_status": "applies", "change_penalty_status": "applies", "flight_link": "https://example.com/flight-details" } } } ``` For inline rows, include `flight_data` inside the row’s `data`. Include these required `flight_data` fields: `id`, `passengers`, and `slices`. Include at least one slice and at least one segment per slice. Include `segments` for each slice. Include `from`, `to`, `depart`, and `arrive` for each segment. All other flight fields shown are optional, including segment `passengers`. Within passenger templates, `type` and `age` are optional. Within segment passengers, `cabin` and `bags` are optional. Within baggage objects, `carry_on` and `checked` are optional. Use nonnegative integers for counts and ages; booleans for `nonstop`, `cabin_varies`, and `baggage_varies`; and strings for other scalar values, including `price`. Set `refundable` and `changeable` to "yes", "no", or "not stated". Omit unknown optional fields rather than passing null. Keep slices and segments in travel order. Use one slice for a one-way trip and two slices for a round trip. Keep connecting flights in their slice's `segments`. Present each complete offer once in one row, from comparison through selection. Do not split outbound and return into separate rows or lists. Treat `price` as the whole trip price for all passengers. Do not invent per-slice prices or combine legs from different offers. Set each segment's `depart` and `arrive` to one airport-local ISO 8601 datetime, such as "2026-09-15T07:35:00", without a timezone suffix. Copy Duffel's segment `departing_at` into `depart` and `arriving_at` into `arrive`. Omit Duffel's display-time strings and the slice-level `depart` and `arrive`. Do not supply formatted timestamps. The server derives slice endpoints and client timestamp strings from the first and last segments. For browser results, obtain the local date and time for every endpoint before creating a flight row. Preserve source duration strings. Preserve known segment cabins and baggage in `segments[].passengers`. The runtime derives cabin and baggage summaries when the detailed facts are complete. Known differences mark variation; missing facts remain unknown. When only source-reported summaries are available, use offer-level `bags` and `slices[].cabin`; retain source-reported `baggage_varies` or `slices[].cabin_varies` when detailed passenger facts are unavailable. Include a slice's source-reported `stops` when technical stops occur within a segment. Otherwise omit it and let the runtime count connections. Preserve each segment's `carrier` name and `flight` number. Put its source IATA or ICAO code in `segments[].carrier_code` when available. Keep codeshare operators separately in `operating_carrier` and `operating_flight`. Omit `response_message`, slice `from` and `to`, offer `stops`, and `nonstop` when authoring flight data. Both input forms receive the same route/stop summaries and an identifying reply before storage. Keep the offer id as the private checkout mapping. The server supplies "Book with <agent_name>" as the CTA when `flight_action` is omitted. When it is present, the server uses its CTA and response prefix while still appending the exact selected itinerary and total. Do not calculate elapsed durations by subtracting airport-local clocks; preserve source durations. Creating a row does not submit it or authorize a purchase. Add `flight_link` only for a verified absolute HTTP(S) details URL. Keep checkout credentials out of the payload.
